messages:
maria: quick thought — do we want the model intake to be fail-fast on any bench regression, or allow a probation state with progressive checks?
aj: fail-fast reduces blast radius but we get false positives from noisy benches. probation lets us gather real traffic metrics.
sanjay: +1 to probation. we saw a model flagged by bench because of tokenization edgecases but it performed fine in canary. wasted cycles.
maria: how long is probation? hours? days? cost adds up.
aj: propose two-tier probation: short (2h) for low-risk models, long (48h) for bigger ones. during probation we run golden probes + 1% canary traffic.
elaine: important: probe mismatch vs user-facing regression are different. our current alert threshold (3% golden mismatch) is too tight for noisy emergent tokens. we need metric smoothing.
sanjay: agree. suggest we use a weighted acceptance score: 40% regressions on golden probes, 30% p95 latency delta, 20% token throughput, 10% qualitative evals. threshold >= 0.7 pass.
maria: weights are arbitrary. who owns tuning them? ops or ml infra?
aj: ML infra should set defaults based on model family, ops can override per-customer.
elaine: operationally we also need a clear rollback trigger during probation. e.g., if user-facing error rate > 0.1% or latency p95 regresses > 50ms, auto-rollback.
sanjay: for rollback we need fast revert in dedicated pools. add a canary circuit-breaker that drops new model traffic instantly.
maria: implementation sketch: intake -> bench smoke -> if baseline pass -> probation state created in registry with probation metadata (duration, canary %, required_score). probation agent collects metrics and updates score. final decision executed by gate service.
aj: question: where does batch/quantization affect bench results? we need bench to run variants (fp16, q4) too, otherwise we accept a model incompatible with production config.
sanjay: run bench matrix: {precision: [fp16,q4], sharding: [single, multi], seq_len: [128,1024]}. but that's combinatorial. do prioritized combinations: common deployment profiles first.
maria: need a budget cap for probation testing to avoid runaway costs. default 5 GPU-hours per probation unless owner requests more.
elaine: telemetry: mark probation runs with a tag so billing and observability exclude them from production baselines. also surface a single "probation report" in console with pass/fail reasons.
aj: small UX ask: console should show an explainable breakdown: which probe failed, sample inputs, stack traces if kernel OOM.
sanjay: edgecase: models that deterministically fail golden probes but pass canary (e.g., hallucination tradeoff). we should allow manual override with documented risk and two approvers.
maria: manual override is fine but should create an audit trail and require a postmortem plan.
elaine: final point — we should run a short A/B for 24h after probation success before full rollout. that reduces surprise regressions.
aj: sounds like consensus: fail-fast still for critical infra issues (OOMs, serialization errors), otherwise probation-with-scorer + staged AB rollout. I'll draft an RFC with the state machine and probation metadata.
onboard-bot: created probation-ticket #PB-4321 for model: repo/model-x, duration: 48h, canary:1%
maria: thanks — please include onboarding checklist items: bench matrix, budget cap, rollback triggers, manual-override policy.
elaine: and a logging contract for kernel-level failures (OOM, bad dtype) so bench results are actionable.
sanjay: I'll prototype the scorer service this week and post results here.
aj: awesome — ping when ready, we can iterate on weights after some runs.
maria: thanks team — this feels actionable.
